_meta: MACE training/validation error tables for the v4 potential, from the training job's own log (A90; corrected A94).
_why_this_file_exists: A89 reported that the held-out force and energy errors quoted in a draft caption appeared nowhere in the ARC pull. A90 transcribed them from the training log, which was not then in the repository. A94: the log is now in the repository, and it holds TWO error tables for two different models. A90 transcribed the stage-two (SWA) table; production MD ran the stage-one model. `errors` below is therefore the stage-one table, and the stage-two table is kept separately, labelled as not used for production.
source_note: MACE 0.3.16 mace_run_train, job 7924966 (ed_data/arc_scripts/htc_train_v4_resume.sh / htc_train_v4.sh: --swa --start_swa=120, --max_num_epochs=200, --seed=1). Values are the log's 'Error-table on TRAIN and VALID', copied verbatim; validation/test_a94_mlip_errors.py re-reads both tables from the log and checks every number here.

production_model.file: models/water_scw_v4.model (water-scw-mace); loaded as water_scw_v4.model by ed_data/arc_a78/scw/run_prod_md_05fs.py and the other production MD drivers
production_model.sha256_source: ARC sha256 prefix dc4a8977 supplied by H. Taylor (A94); full digest = the git-LFS oid of models/water_scw_v4.model in water-scw-mace, recomputed locally and identical

valid_Default.role: held-out validation split of the production (stage-one) model -- the honest generalisation error of the potential that ran the MD

train_Default.role: training split of the production (stage-one) model

stage_two_not_used_for_production.note: NOT the production potential. Production MD loaded water_scw_v4.model (sha256 dc4a8977...), which differs from water_scw_v4_stagetwo.model (sha256 380e20a8...). A90 transcribed THIS table as the production model's error; A94 withdrew that.
stage_two_not_used_for_production.sha256_source: ARC sha256 prefix supplied by H. Taylor (A94); the full digest is not in either repository

not_to_be_confused_with.distinction: those are TRAINING-SET parity BY REGIME (bulk vs RCB conditions), which reference.json itself calls 'optimistic vs true held-out error', with frames above 3000 K excluded. They are a different quantity from the held-out split error here, not a competing estimate of it.
not_to_be_confused_with.computed_with: the production (stage-one) model, sha256 dc4a8977... -- reproduced in A94, see reproduction_a94

reproduction_a94.what: models/water_scw_v4.model (sha256 dc4a8977d44e...) evaluated on every frame of water-scw-mace benchmarks/reference/train_v4.xyz.gz (1193 frames, train + valid together; labels from the extxyz energy=/forces fields), CPU, float64, MACE 0.3.16. Regimes as benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py:regime_of (bulk T <= 2250 K, rcb 2250 < T <= 3000 K, T > 3000 K excluded).
reproduction_a94.reading: Energy RMSE over all frames 23.28 matches the stage-one log tables mixed 90/10 (sqrt(0.9*23.5^2 + 0.1*20.8^2) = 23.2), and is 3.5x the stage-two value: the shipped model is stage one. Force parity 41.0 / 58.3 by regime reproduces reference.json's 41 / 58, so reference.json was computed with this same production model. Most of the energy error is a uniform offset (mean -18.9 meV/atom), which does not enter forces or the MD.

lda_note: the only held-out parity inside the pull; belongs to the LDA model, not the production potential
